messages:
alice: quick heads-up — after landing the 'external cuda-graph capture' change I'm seeing tail latency spikes on 8-GPU runs. throughput drops ~20% and some requests hang until all-reduce completes.
ben: which PR/commit? i rolled back PR #842 on staging earlier today (the one that moves kv-prefetch into a capture).
alice: rollback helped but didn't fully restore steady-state. i reproduced locally with small fixture: tp=2 pp=4 batch=16 kv_warmup=4. when kv cache warms, a subset of streams appear idle while others block on all-reduce. attached a tiny nsight trace excerpt:
```
[GPU0][stream3] kernel load_kv_prefetch start 0.0012s duration 0.0018s
[GPU0][stream0] allreduce start 0.0020s duration 0.0035s
[GPU0][stream3] wait event E1 0.0023s
[GPU0][stream0] record event E1 0.0021s
[GPU0][stream3] kernel resumes 0.0060s
```
These timings look reversed: stream3 waits for an event that is recorded later in time on stream0 (but on capture/replay the ordering seems wrong).
caroline: we changed the batcher to try to overlap KV prefetch on a dedicated stream and then capture that stream into the cuda-graph for replay. on replay the capture binds kernel->stream ordering differently. Could be a capture semantics mismatch where recorded host ordering != replay device ordering.
ben: i can reproduce with repro script. running `python tools/repro/comm_overlap.py --gpus 8 --tp 2 --pp 4 --batch 16 --kv-warmup 4` shows the same stall pattern.
dmitri: my initial hunch: cross-stream event dependencies aren't portable into the graph the way we expect. cudaGraph capture can hoist kernels onto the default stream during instantiation, which breaks our explicit event sync assumptions. we should look for missed `cudaGraphAddEventNode` usage or implicit host-device syncs.
alice: good call. i'll add explicit event nodes around KV prefetch and before all-reduce to force ordering in the graph. also going to capture a CUPTI timeline to verify device-side ordering vs host trace.
ben: quick mitigation: disable graph capture for any capture that references events recorded on another stream. easiest is an assert in the capture verifier that rejects cross-stream event dependencies (fail closed).
dmitri: agree — fail closed for now. long-term: implement explicit event nodes in graph creation path, or change batching so kv-prefetch is captured on the same stream as the subsequent all-reduce.
caroline: note: kernel selection heuristics add another wrinkle — on smaller batches we pick smaller kernels that reduce compute time, which increases the relative cost of all-reduce and makes the overlap fragil. profiling shows compute time drops from 2.8ms -> 1.1ms, all-reduce stays ~2.5ms, so any ordering bug is amplified.
ben: PR incoming: #889 adds capture-time check + opt-out flag `--no-cuda-graph-for-crossstream` and a repro unit that runs on 4 GPUs. pushing now.
deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-15T10:12:00Z triggered by PR #842 (commit abc123) to staging.
alice: thanks. i'll validate the patch on large-scale cluster tomorrow morning and collect CUPTI traces. if we still see mismatch we'll disable graph replay for the affected graph shapes.
dmitri: also adding a short-term metrics alert to detect >5% increase in per-request tail when graph capture is enabled so we can roll back faster.
ben: ack, adding the alert and small test.
alice: perfect. lets sync 9am PT tomorrow with traces. :thumbsup:
